newsitem.title: USA: Muni dealers laud U.S. balanced budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Muni dealers laud U.S. balanced budget pact.

text.p: PSA The Bond Market Trade Association called the balanced budget pact reached on Friday by the White House and congressional Republican leaders a "very positive development."

"In general, a balanced budget is going to be good for all of the bond markets. Everybody in the bond markets should be happy about," Michael Decker, PSA vice president of policy analysis, said in a telephone interview following a press briefing on the new agreement to balance the U.S. federal budget by 2002.

Friday's pact does not specify such details as whether or not Congress will adopt President Clinton's controversial proposal to repeal the two percent "de minimis" rule on corporate holdings of tax-exempt bonds.
That proposal is strongly opposed by bond dealers and issuers who warn its adoption will raise the costs of tax- exempt borrowing and leasing by localities and hamper infrastructure financing.
Decker said Congress will not make decisions on whether or not to adopt that and other budget specifics until this summer.
"There's a whole menu of stuff that's going to be before the House Ways and Means Committee and Senate Finance Committee," Decker said.
Panels can choose to reject the de minimis repeal proposal as long as they can substitute in other cuts that would raise enough revenues to balance the budget, he said.
